summary: MF-025: collapse active_tickets, closed_tickets and ticket_phase into one ticket_state ordinal (0..5). Premise re-verified with TLC in both directions. Retention exact: 9,011 distinct / depth 24 / 87,464 generated, unchanged. Declared bound measured 663,552 -> 34,992 (18.96x).

assertions: the three variables are gone and ticket_state carries the lifecycle.
reachable distinct states remain 9,011 and depth remains 24, matching the MF-014 baseline exactly; the baseline is established on-branch first and divergence in EITHER direction stops the ticket.
derived operators ActiveTickets and ClosedTickets are defined so every set-valued reader still reads a set; the model reads as a lifecycle, not arithmetic on an integer.

every invariant and guard has an equivalent over ticket_state, with the before/after mapping enumerated; invariants that become structurally true are RETAINED BY NAME per the MF-020 and MF-022 precedent.
no adapter references a removed variable.
if a reachable combination is found that does not fit the six, the ticket STOPS and reports -- that finding means the premise is wrong and the collapse must not proceed.
the declared bound drop is measured and reported separately from any other change.
commands: python3 scripts/tla_spec_dev.py --spec-root specs run spec-unit-tests --ticket MF-025
results: PREMISE RE-VERIFIED against the model rather than trusted: TLC confirms both directions on the pre-collapse model. No seventh combination -- a SixCombinationsOnly invariant holds across all 9,011 reachable states -- and each of the six ordinals is individually reachable (six negated-reachability probes all violated). The three variables genuinely are one totally ordered lifecycle, so the collapse is a faithful re-representation and not a packing trick.

RETENTION: on-branch pre-collapse baseline MEASURED before editing (not quoted from MF-014): 9,011 distinct states, depth 24, 87,464 generated. Post-collapse: 9,011 distinct, depth 24, 87,464 generated, identical outdegree profile (avg 1, max 8, p95 6). Equal in both directions. The matching generated-state count is stronger than the distinct/depth gate alone -- a deleted self-loop would show as a generated-states drop at constant distinct states, and there is none.

REDUCTION MEASURED: declared bound 663,552 -> 34,992 (18.96x), bounded dimensions 7 -> 5, variables 9 -> 7. The ticket's DERIVED projection was ~34,992; the measured value is 34,992 exactly, so projection and measurement agree. The measured value is what is recorded.

READABILITY: derived operators ActiveTickets == {t \\in Tickets : ticket_state[t] \\in TicketOpened..TicketSpecUnitTestsPassed} and ClosedTickets == {t \\in Tickets : ticket_state[t] = TicketClosed} are defined and used at every set-valued site, alongside named stage constants TicketUnopened/TicketOpened/TicketDesiredReady/TicketCurrentReady/TicketSpecUnitTestsPassed/TicketClosed, so guards and invariants read as a lifecycle rather than as arithmetic on an integer.

All 12 invariants retained BY NAME; MC.cfg unchanged. NoOpenClosedOverlap, ClosedTicketsPassedSpecUnitTests and the TypeInvariant subset conjuncts are now structurally true and retained anyway per the MF-020/MF-022 precedent.

SUBTLE MAPPING recorded in mapping.md: the two gate invariants quantified over ticket_phase[t] >= 3, which closed tickets also satisfied because CloseTicket left the phase at 3. The faithful equivalent is >= TicketSpecUnitTestsPassed (states 4 AND 5), not an equality -- an equality would have weakened both gates. Likewise RunSpecUnitTests keeps a RANGE guard (states 3..4) rather than an equality, preserving the idempotent re-run self-loop; a regression test pins it.

NEW FINDING referred to MF-023, not worked around: the collapse dissolved component C2 (which was exactly the three lifecycle variables), so ticket_state joins C1 and modularity Q falls 0.022 -> 0.000. analyze complexity now also reports 'C1 has 7 variables, exceeding max_component_variables 6' alongside the pre-existing 'C1 is touched by 12 actions'. This is a metric artifact of the merge rather than increased coupling -- three mutually coupled variables became one. Both are C1 decomposition problems, which is MF-023's scope. The budget gate was already FAIL before this ticket, so its pass/fail state is unchanged.

Refinement search: SEARCHED, FOUND NONE in scope. ticket_state cannot shrink (all six ordinals shown reachable); setup_phase/spec_root/complexity_gate/corpus_gate are each already at reachable cardinality. Residual slack (9,011 actual vs 34,992 bound, 25.8% density) is cross-variable correlation, not single-variable over-declaration, and would need a dependent representation -- the deferred MF-018 direction. lastCommand/result projection remains deferred to MF-016 and would not move the bound anyway, since both are already excluded from it as unconstrained.

Validations DEFERRED to MF-023 per the epic-wide instruction: spec-case generation, corpus run, effect conformance, and mutation kill test. The known 'C1 touched by 12 actions' finding was not worked around.

implementation_scope: specs/current/tests (adapter assertions referencing the removed variables)
ticket.objective: Owner-approved architectural move, third instance of the pattern after MF-020 and MF-022. Replace active_tickets (SUBSET Tickets), closed_tickets (SUBSET Tickets) and ticket_phase ([Tickets -> 0..3]) with a single ticket_state in [Tickets -> 0..5]. These are not independent facts but one per-ticket lifecycle recorded three ways -- 0 unopened, 1..4 active at phases 0..3, 5 closed. VERIFIED against the model before scheduling, which is what makes this a faithful re-representation rather than a packing trick -- OpenTicket guards on the ticket being in neither set so it is never reopened and the lifecycle is monotonic; CloseTicket leaves ticket_phase UNCHANGED so a closed ticket retains phase 3 and there is no closed-with-other-phase state; NoOpenClosedOverlap already forbids being both. Exactly six per-ticket combinations are reachable and they are totally ordered. Declared representation 8 x 8 x 64 = 4,096 becomes 6^3 = 216, a factor of 18.96 derived from the model, projecting bound 663,552 -> ~34,992 which must be MEASURED on-branch not quoted. Scheduled now rather than later because each gate ticket triples the bound and the next one breaches the 1,000,000 budget; the standing objective answers a bad measurement with an architecture change, not a raised budget. See tickets/025-ticket-state-collapse.md.
